P1.evidence: The only call in this batch where the opening frame was actually set, and it was set cleanly in a single move: 'I want to understand your situation better. What are your goals? Where are you trying to get to? What have you tried in the past? And how we can actually help you with that?' That is a four-part frame with past attempts substituted for what's in the way, followed immediately by explicit frame agreement — 'And if there's a way we can help, I can tell you exactly how we can run this. Sounds good?' P1a is N/A: there is no setter and no application to read back.

P2.evidence: Height, current weight and target weight were all asked directly; age never was. Work was covered properly including the sitting question, the hours and the hybrid split. The injury probe was thorough and correctly sequenced: 'do you have any injuries or anything that limits your movements?', then 'Did you have surgery on that?', then 'do you have pain of that ACL?', then 'does it show up every day?', then a sweep for anything else — 'Any pains? Any stiffness?'. Training week was asked and produced honest variance ('three days a week, maybe I increase to four, maybe decrease to two'). Diet was asked and followed up on processed food and favourite food. Health conditions were never asked at all, own or hereditary. Sleep and energy were never asked. Results from the current self-directed training were volunteered, not asked.

P3.evidence: The structural moves were mostly attempted. The bridge ran — 'in your own words, what's the biggest reason you want to actually lose this weight and achieve your goals?' — and the future-worth question ran well: 'imagine yourself getting married, being slimmer, being like 70-74 kilos, and actually being stronger for daily life. So when you think about it, what becomes possible for you? What would that moment be worth to you?'. The 'what are you missing out on' probe at 00:14:06 is a good version of P3c. Where it falls down is depth. The answers coming back were thin and partly a language artefact, and instead of slowing down or rephrasing, the rep let the thread drift into an extended rapport tangent about how many children he wants and whether boys or girls, including an anecdote about his own father showing him the belt. No reflect-back of the form 'so this isn't really about the weight' was ever attempted, which is a significant omission on a call where the surface goal is explicitly a wedding photograph.

P4.evidence: The tightest phase on the call. Past attempts were asked directly ('Have you tried anything in the past to solve that? Have you trained with a trainer or followed any plan?') and produced the full history — gym membership, time made it impossible, bought home equipment instead. The root-cause question was asked in almost exactly the scripted form: 'can I ask you, like, why cannot you do it by yourself? Like, you're already working out. So why cannot you be consistent by yourself?' That is P4f delivered properly, and it worked — the prospect named his own gap without prompting: 'I need my trainer to organize the plan... What about the right movements to be in a good position, to prevent from my injury?'

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was skipped in its entirety. Not one of the four moves was attempted in any form. This is the most striking omission on the call because the lever was already on the table — a fixed, dated, emotionally loaded deadline four months out — and the cost of arriving at his own wedding unchanged was never once put to him. The rep referenced the deadline only as a logistics constraint on programme length: 'we don't have much time because the marriage is in October.'

P6.evidence: P6a was asked in proper form — 'if you had the right training, the right nutrition, and accountability from Trevor, all built around your life, do you agree that you would get to your goals and lose this weight for your marriage?' — but the prospect's first response was 'You're asking about what?', and the rep repeated it before getting 'I will achieve this with you, surely.' P6b was delivered as an assertion rather than the scripted question: 'So I understand that you are fully committed to showing up and doing the work, which is going to be difficult, but it's going to be successful. Yes?' The 'is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' formulation never ran. P6c is partial rather than hit because a yes obtained on the second reading of a question the prospect did not understand the first time is not the clear yes the script is asking for.

P11.evidence: ASSESSMENT LIMITED BY TRUNCATION — the recording ends at 00:33:13 and anything after that point is unknown. On the audible portion: the payment step was started properly, with method established and the link put in the Zoom chat and confirmed received, but no payment was taken and the prospect then asked to pay after the session. The Trevor onboarding call was described but not scheduled, no slots were offered, and neither the agreement email nor the welcome email, Skool link or onboarding questionnaire were mentioned at any point.

objection_plays.detail: UNASSESSABLE RATHER THAN GENUINELY MISSED. The only money-adjacent moment on the call arrives at 00:32:49 — 'Can I pay after this session? Because I will adjust some regarding to the payment' — and the recording cuts twenty-four seconds later with the rep still asking him to repeat it. Scored miss because nothing ran on the recording, but a human should treat this as unknown rather than as a rep failure. No other objection of any kind was raised in the thirty-three audible minutes: no price resistance, no think-about-it, no spouse, no timing, no fear.

notes: A genuinely mixed call. P1 is the best in the batch and P4 is close behind — the opening frame with agreement, and 'why cannot you be consistent by yourself?', are both worth lifting as examples. P5 was skipped completely, which on a call with a fixed wedding date four months out is the largest single missed opportunity in this batch. The coaching priority, though, is not a phase. The prospect asked the rep to repeat himself at least four times, answered the commitment check with 'You're asking about what?', and told him outright 'I didn't recognize your question well' — and the rep's pace, vocabulary and idiom ('rock and roll', 'guilty pleasure', 'teach you how to fish') never changed. Whatever the score says about phases run, comprehension was not established before a $6,000 commitment was taken, and the four-month-versus-six-month arithmetic was raised by the rep himself and then dropped.
